@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: 9a80
+title: Consumer-visible input token usage is always zero, because the usage channel send is disabled
+---
+Reported by the `FoundationModelsRouter` and `FoundationModelsMultitool`
+sessions, from two independent read paths, on 2026-08-14. Localized in this
+repository the same day.
+
+## What the consumers see
+
+Surface 1, `FoundationModelsRouter`, reads `Usage` off a completed turn
+(`LanguageModelSessionBackendTests.swift`), against Muse Glimmer:
+
+- `:541` `turn1Usage.input.totalTokenCount > 0` — FAILED, on the FIRST turn
+- `:563` `turn2Usage.input.cachedTokenCount > 0` — FAILED
+- `:574` `abs(turn2Usage.input.cachedTokenCount - turn1ProcessedTokenCount) <= tolerance` — FAILED
+
+Surface 2, `FoundationModelsMultitool`, reads
+`SessionEvent.turnEnded(TokenUsage)` off the event stream:
+
+```
+tokens=TokenUsage(tokensIn: 0, tokensOut: 347, contextFill: 0.00264739990234375)
+```
+
+That turn made five tool calls and spliced a full discovery catalog, thus
+the input was large. The output count of 347 is correct.
+
+## The cause, and it is already written in the source
+
+`Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift:721` `emitUsage` does
+NOT send usage to the FoundationModels channel. It gives usage to the
+`generationObserver` task-local alone, which only a test reads. The comment
+at `:752` says the effect word for word:
+
+> Effect: the framework does not receive our per-response usage event, so
+> consumer-visible usage for these responses may be absent or zero. Tests
+> still observe usage through `generationObserver` above.
+
+The reason is an SDK symbol drift, recorded at `:729`. The FM-27 beta
+`.swiftinterface` declares `Response.Action.updateUsage(input:output:metadata:)`
+with three parameters. The shipping FoundationModels dylib exports the older
+two-parameter `updateUsage(input:output:)`. Our call took the `metadata:`
+default, thus the compiler bound the three-parameter symbol, which does not
+exist at run time. Under chained fixups that aborts the process at image
+load; under lazy binding it faults through null the moment the send runs.
+A `dlsym` guard does not help, because the compiled reference alone is
+enough to abort. Thus the send was removed.
+
+## Why the input side alone looks wrong
+
+This is the part the reports could not see, and it explains the asymmetry
+exactly.
+
+The framework counts the OUTPUT tokens itself, because it receives them.
+Nobody but this repository can know the INPUT count, and this repository
+does not send it. Thus:
+
+- output — correct, and it comes from the framework, not from us
+- input — zero, because no value ever arrives
+
+Thus `tokensIn: 0` is not an input-specific defect. It is the whole usage
+event that never arrives, and the output number hides that.
+
+`contextFill` at 0.0026 is small and non-zero, thus the framework computes
+it from something of its own.
+
+Every one of the five `emitUsage` call sites also hard-codes
+`cachedTokenCount: 0` (`:1423`, `:1642`, `:1732`, `:1781`, `:1974`). That is
+a second defect under the first: even after the send is restored, the cached
+count stays 0 and the two `cachedTokenCount` assertions above stay red.
+
+## The work
+
+- [ ] Tell whether the shipping SDK now exports
+      `updateUsage(input:output:metadata:)`. Read the macOS 27 SDK
+      `.swiftinterface` AND the dylib exports; the whole defect is that the
+      two disagreed
+- [ ] If they agree, restore the send that `:757` records
+- [ ] If they still disagree, find a way to reach the two-parameter symbol
+      without a compile-time reference to the three-parameter one
+- [ ] Give `cachedTokenCount` a real value at each of the five call sites.
+      `GenerateCompletionInfo` and the prompt-cache path hold the number of
+      tokens reuse skipped
+- [ ] Add a test that reads usage through the CHANNEL, not through
+      `generationObserver`. The observer path passes today and hides this
+
+## Scope
+
+`MLXFoundationModels` is neither DeepSeek-V4 nor MiniMax work. The
+`catch-up-upstream` branch holds its difference against `main` to those two
+alone, thus this card waits for the user. #eventplan
\ No newline at end of file

forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -1,6 +1,67 @@
 ---
 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m02fsas5cy5kkt1d2q5p01pk
+  text: |
+    ### The dylib was measured. The symbol drift is GONE.
+
+    Measured on macOS 27.0, build 26A5388g, on 2026-08-15. The comment at
+    `MLXLanguageModel.swift:729` says the interface and the shipping dylib
+    disagree. On this build they AGREE, and they agree on the three-parameter
+    form.
+
+    | View | What it holds |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | `.swiftinterface` (what the compiler reads) | the 3-parameter `updateUsage(input:output:metadata:)`, `metadata` with a default. NO 2-parameter overload. |
+    | `FoundationModels.tbd` (what the linker reads) | 3 symbols, each with `8metadata` in the mangled name |
+    | **the runtime dylib** (what dyld binds) | **the SAME 3 symbols, each with `8metadata`** |
+
+    The runtime read comes from `dyld_info -exports` against
+    `/System/Library/Frameworks/FoundationModels.framework/Versions/A/FoundationModels`,
+    which resolves through the dyld shared cache. It gives real addresses
+    (`0x000D2B5C`, `0x000D40BC`, `0x000D4018`), thus it read the true image.
+
+    Demangled, one of the three:
+
+    ```
+    static FoundationModels.LanguageModelExecutorGenerationChannel.Response.Action
+      .updateUsage(
+        input: ...Usage.Input,
+        output: ...Usage.Output,
+        metadata: [Swift.String : Swift.Decodable & Swift.Encodable
+                   & Swift.Equatable & Swift.Sendable])
+      -> ...Response.Action
+    ```
+
+    **A count of the exports that hold `updateUsage` and NOT `metadata`: 0.**
+
+    Thus the two-parameter symbol that the comment names does not exist in the
+    interface, in the linker stub, or in the runtime. The three-parameter
+    symbol exists in all three. The compiler binds what the runtime exports.
+
+    ### What this changes
+
+    The reason the send was removed does not hold on this build. Either a later
+    system update corrected the drift, or the first reading of it was not
+    correct. This measurement does not say which, and it does not need to.
+
+    The first work item of this card is answered: the shipping SDK DOES export
+    `updateUsage(input:output:metadata:)`.
+
+    ### What still needs proof
+
+    A symbol table says the symbol exists. It does not say the whole send
+    works. The empirical proof is to restore the four lines that `:757`
+    records and run the `MLXFoundationModelsTests` suite. If the image loads
+    and the suite passes, dyld bound the symbol. If the old defect were still
+    present, the process would abort at image load, thus the test run is itself
+    the measurement.
+
+    That step needs the user, because `MLXFoundationModels` is outside the
+    scope rule of this branch.
+  timestamp: 2026-08-15T10:34:22.885769+00:00

 position_ordinal: 9a80

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m02kp8576j1ja4a39dza9j96
+  text: |-
+    ### Re-measured on macOS 27.0 build 26A5406e, Xcode 27.0 (27A5237l), 2026-08-15
+
+    The user updated Xcode and macOS. The earlier reading was on build 26A5388g,
+    thus this is a fresh measurement on the newer system.
+
+    **The `updateUsage` symbol still agrees across all three views.**
+
+    ```
+    dyld_info -exports .../FoundationModels | grep -c updateUsage        -> 6
+    ... | grep updateUsage | grep -c 8metadata                           -> 6
+    ```
+
+    Six symbols now (the SDK added `Reasoning` and `ToolCalls` action variants),
+    and every one of them carries `metadata`. A count of `updateUsage` exports
+    WITHOUT `metadata` is still 0. Thus the restored send is correct on this
+    build too.
+
+    **Empirical proof is now in hand.** `swift test` ran the whole in-package
+    suite with the send restored:
+
+    - 814 tests / 68 suites — passed
+    - 69 tests / 14 suites — passed
+    - 140 tests / 22 suites — passed
+    - 7 tests / 5 suites — passed
+    - 0 failures
+
+    The image loaded and every suite ran, thus dyld bound the three-parameter
+    symbol. Work item 1 and work item 2 of this card are done.
+
+    **One correction to the record above.** The demangled signature recorded in
+    the prior comment is stale. The metadata VALUE type changed in this SDK:
+
+    | Build | `metadata` value type |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | 26A5388g | `[String : Decodable & Encodable & Equatable & Sendable]` |
+    | 26A5406e | `[String : any ConvertibleToGeneratedContent]` |
+
+    That change broke the build, and the fix is in the same commit as this
+    comment.
+
+    **Still open:** give `cachedTokenCount` a real value at the five call sites
+    (`:1423`, `:1642`, `:1732`, `:1781`, `:1974`), and add a test that reads
+    usage through the CHANNEL rather than through `generationObserver`.
